speaker: stephanieasher
text: Well, welcome back, everybody. Apologies for the technical issues. This is part of the reason that we ran a trial for the virtual Council meetings. Now, it won't change anything as far as the debate and the decision-making goes tonight with the meeting. It's just that we're not in the same room. We are streaming online as usual, and you may also have noticed that we have a few extra faces tonight among the 11 Councillors. So, welcome, a very special welcome to our Junior Mayor and Deputy Mayor. Ashley Delaney will be presenting the report tonight, and they're both representing the Youth Council. So, this will be the second report from the group this year, and we're really delighted to have them with us. We just wish we could have them in the Chamber, so maybe another time in the very near future we can have our Junior Councillors in the Chamber with us. Now, regarding the agenda tonight, it is quite a small agenda. We do try and manage the flow of business through the CEO and the Director of Governance. We have had quite a few really big Council meetings, and the June 30 meeting, which is our next one, is also a very full agenda. Do we have any apologies for this evening? I don't think we do. Everybody's here. Do we have any requests for leaves of absence from Councillors tonight? No, we don't. Okay, thank you. Getting used to the rhythm of the hands on the screen. Now, do we have any declarations of conflict of interest this evening? With quite a short agenda, I don't imagine that we do, so no, thank you very much. If any do arise during the meeting, please make them known. Now, public question and submission time. We have continued to accept questions and submissions to Council online, and I'd like to note tonight that we do have an amendment to our public question and submission time policy to guide us through this period of COVID-19. We've received six questions and submissions for tonight's meeting. Each person has now received a response via email, and it's also important to note that each Councillor has read every question and submission sent in. Thank you to the following people who have sent in submissions or questions for tonight. We've had questions from Vicki Perrett, Sally Fisher, Neil Plummer, Sanya Van Heuwet, Karen Campbell, and Noreen Nicholson, so thank you to those people, and they have received answers already. Now, do we have any petitions for this evening? I'd like to now ask Ashley to present the Youth Council's second report, so welcome, Ashley.

speaker: juniormayor
text: Councillor Ashley Delaney. Hello, everyone. Before I begin, I would like to acknowledge the Wathaurong people, the traditional owners of this land, and pay my respects to their Elders past, present, and emerging, as well as acknowledging all Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people present this evening. Good evening, Mayor Stephanie Asher, Greater Geelong Councillors and Directors, Youth Councillors, and everyone else streaming at home. My name is Ashley Delaney, and I am the Junior Deputy Mayor for the Youth Council. Tonight, I will outline the progress and achievements of the Youth Council since our last report. These last few months have looked very different for all of us, and I am happy to say that the Youth Council was still able to meet virtually during these challenging times. This has allowed us to complete all of our expectations and goals the Youth Council would usually discuss and accomplish in our monthly meetings. Over the last few months, we've achieved many things we would like to share. In our April meeting on Zoom, we were lucky enough to have two presentations, one about the Eldershot Reserve concept plan, and another on Council's social infrastructure plan. The Youth Council was able to provide advice that focused on helping young people in our community benefit from these plans as much as possible. The Youth Council were able to come together to vote on both the native vegetation mascot naming competition, as well as the postcard competition. We are especially proud that the winning postcard design would be sent to isolated members in our community, hopefully bringing joy in a time of much uncertainty and hardship. The Youth Council have also been discussing ways to communicate and engage with the community. We are excited to use the Youth Engagement app, which will be a great way for us to get feedback, opinions and information from young people we are representing. The Youth Council Instagram account has also recently been created with the plans to produce content that engages with the Geelong community. These platforms will be our best and most effective form of communication to engage with the large number of young people, hopefully meaning we can reach a lot more of the Geelong community. Finally, one of the many privileges that the Geelong Youth Council have had since our last report is the chance to be involved in choosing the categories for the 2020 Geelong Youth Awards. The Youth Council chose six categories including Youth Educator, Equality Award, Leadership slash Positive Role Model, Diverse Cultural Contribution, Art and Music, Disability Inclusion Award. These categories were voted with the priorities and views of the Youth Council and nominations to recognise the amazing young people in our community close on Friday 19th of June. To help promote the awards, the junior mayor interviewed by the Pulse community radio station and the deputy junior mayor recorded a voiceover advertisement used to promote the awards on the Pulse. Using the information and feedback the Youth Council has received in these and other interactions over the past two months, we would like to use this report as a chance to offer feedback to our council. Firstly, an interesting and concerning point was made at our April meeting regarding the lack of social infrastructure in the Geelong community that is fully dedicated to our youth. The fort, which is a regional facility that provides free programs and safe spaces for young people to relax, socialise and interact with other young people in our community, is located in the Windermere Ward and is the only fully dedicated youth infrastructure in our city. It was brought forward by Youth Council members the importance of the fort and the benefits we would see if there was an increase in youth infrastructure in the Geelong community. Youth Council were impressed by the city's draft social infrastructure plan and agreed that there should be additional dedicated and integrated youth drop-in spaces across the Geelong region. With this in mind, Youth Council would like to advocate that council invest in the creation of fort-like facilities in all council wards across the Geelong local government areas. Secondly, mental health is an issue that not only impacts our community but the world today. We acknowledge the amazing work done to date by the council as this is an issue that the Youth Council is very passionate about and one of our priorities for 2020. We feel that there needs to be more done in the community regarding mental health acknowledgement and understanding for young people. The council's youth development unit provides mental health first aid courses that have been rolled out in some Geelong secondary schools and we see this as a great start to improving this issue. However, we do feel that it is crucial for all schools in Geelong to have this program to see the true benefit as after restrictions are lifted, mental health will be a critical issue for young people. After discussing the importance of this issue, Youth Council would like to advocate that additional youth development staff are trained in mental health first aid. Also, Youth Council would like to suggest that council publicly encourage all schools to take up the opportunity provided by council as a matter of urgency. As we move forward and prepare for our next report, Youth Council's focus will continue to collaborate with more young people and to utilise the digital engagement tools that we have available to us. We believe this is especially important during these times of uncertainty. The Youth Council will continue to meet monthly to discuss ideas, proposals and provide advice to council to better the Geelong community and help have a positive impact. We will continue to learn from those around us and share our thoughts through the Councillor Connect mentoring program sessions. We are excited to have respectful and interesting discussions with our ward councillors to understand their views on issues that are important to us. To conclude, the Geelong Youth Council have been working very hard over the last two months and have faced challenges regarding COVID-19, but we have been able to work through these together. The next report to council will be on Tuesday 25 August with another update on our work,

When we're regarding the ratepayers' dollar, we should always be on top of if we are getting the most value for our ratepayers' money, but I will just put out there that a review into this may actually reinforce the effectiveness of the committee and reinforce the good work that they do do. So, I shouldn't believe that this should be taken as a negative aspect of connotation or suggestion, but really just making sure that we are crossing all the T's and dotting all the I's to get the best bang that we can. With that, I will just say that I am supportive of this recommendation. Councillor MARX

I think the marketing possibly would become a little bit broader in its focus, and also with the proposed tool that has been put together with Brand Geelong, I think there's a whole new approach that could be reviewed here, whether or not it goes that far, but certainly I'd like to see that side of it explored to see whether there can be a broader application and benefit to the region. Councillor MARX Thank you, Councillor MONAIN.

speaker: stephanieasher
text: Great, thank you, Councillor MURPHY. On that note, we'll put the recommendation to the vote. All those in favour? Those against? Carried. On to the last item, which is the Council meeting during COVID-19 and an update to the public question and submission time policy. That's a bit of a mouthful. Now, I'm going to move this one, and I believe Councillor GRISBECK is going to second. Thank you. Now, this is actually updating our policy for public questions and submissions in the Chamber, in line with recent changes to the Local Government Act. In April, the Victorian Government passed the Omnibus, which enacted temporary changes to the Local Government Act, specifically relating to the COVID-19 pandemic response and how we can actually conduct Council meetings. This is our first session, as I said, about the virtual meetings. Since the lockdown, we've had the Council meetings without members of the public in the gallery, but we have live-streamed the meetings and continue to do that, and we do publish recordings of the meetings online. Public questions and submissions to Council have also been received online, as usual, and it's been something that we've been discussing in detail, because we do recognise that people do really appreciate the opportunity to ask questions and to come into the gallery. So, it's not a decision that we ever take lightly. We do agonise over how we can do that effectively, but community safety during the lockdown was obviously the priority, and also following the restrictions set by the State Government. So, the public question and submission time policy has now been updated to reflect those temporary amendments that have been introduced by what is the Emergency Measures Act and the Ministerial Guidelines as well. So, without going into any more detail, I might let Councillor GRISBECK talk to this one a little bit too, and then we can go from there. Councillor GRISBECK. Councillor GRISBECK I might just reserve my right at the moment, Madam Mayor, please. Chair Absolutely. Is anyone else interested in having a conversation about this one? Councillor COUNTILL. Councillor COUNTILL I apologise.

speaker: eddykontel
text: Thanks, Madam Mayor. Supportive of the report, and look, I guess any changes that can happen in an environment that still ensures the safety and health of our community, but starts to lead us to a road of normalisation, I applaud. But the sooner that we can allow the public back into the Chamber, watching the debates live, having them participate live, going through the questions and being able to speak to those, whether that be that they disagree with what we're doing, that they bring suggestions forward or requiring answers, I think it couldn't be quick enough. I think the community has done a great job working with us, as has the Council, to try to adapt to the circumstances that have been forced upon us. But there's no doubt that, as Councillors, I'm pretty sure I can speak for all of us, that the sooner that we can see the community back in the Chamber engaging with us as we once remember it, the better it will be for not only the Council, but for the city of Greater Geelong.

speaker: stephanieasher
text: Chair Absolutely agree, Councillor COUNTILL. Councillor MANSFIELD.

speaker: sarahmansfield
text: Councillor MANSFIELD Thank you, Mayor Asha. I similarly am really finding the lack of question time at the beginning of our meetings as it's really taken something away from the meetings. I thank those community members who continue to submit questions and appreciate that it's definitely not the same thing when you can't be there to ask your question. Given time restrictions on our face-to-face meetings, we haven't even really had the opportunity to read them out or respond to them in the way that we normally would. Some of that has been really the response to the State Government requirements around social distancing and a desire to keep the community as safe as possible, but absolutely agree. The sooner we can find a way to safely have community members participate in our meetings again, the better. It really, I think, is one of the more important parts of our meetings and it's a really important way for the community to have their voice heard. There's nothing quite like having members of the community come up and ask us questions and keep us all to account in that public arena. So, I support this report, but as Councillor CONTELL has said, can't wait to have the community back in the Chamber, once again, holding us to account. Councillor AITKEN.

speaker: stephanieasher
text: Councillor AITKEN. Hear, hear. Well said, Councillor MANSFIELD. Do we have any other comments on this particular item? This is the last one for the night. So, Councillor AITKEN. Councillor AITKEN.

speaker: anthonyaitken
text: Thank you, Mayor Asher. Yeah, look, I echo the same words as what everybody else has said as well, too. We all are missing public question time. I personally, I actually love the theatre of local government and local politics and one of the important parts of that theatre is actually having the community with you, in front of you, and also having the community present their questions to you. This Council has actually been very successful in embracing public question time and allowing the community into the decision-making process that we are part of as Councillors. I'm really proud of how that was led by the former Mayor, Councillor HOWARD. So, if you don't withstand Councillor HOWARD, the legacy that you've left in this Council has been really good for public question time. I thank you for that and I thank the current Mayor for continuing on that legacy that Councillor HOWARD has created about engaging with the community during public question time. Public question time is really good to provide sunlight on local government. Our officers don't enjoy public question time as much as what we do as Councillors, because the community essentially is wanting to get some answers and usually a number of the questions that they're presenting to us are quite strong. For Kylie and I, public question time and engagement with the community has been really important with some issues for us. The goat issue in Lara would not have reached the same success that it did if we didn't have public question time and the ability for the community to participate in the decision-making process. It's the same as well, too, with the illegal waste dumping facility in Broderick Road as well, too. They were very much—the community was able to strongly put their views about those issues and remind the Council of our responsibility and assist us with the decisions that we ultimately made in those areas. So, I endorse all the words that have been spoken by all the other Councillors at this point in time. We miss it. Hopefully, it will return when COVID-19 formal restrictions are off and the theatre of local government and local politics can be centre stage again at City Hall and our community focus meetings, because we must also remember that our community focus meetings where we took these meetings out into our community have been really successful as well, too, but COVID-19 has meant we haven't been able to do that. So, it wasn't just giving people a chance to ask questions. It was also taking the meetings out to places like Anarchy and St Leonard's that had never had Council meetings before and they were quite successful. I look forward to some of those really good initiatives that this Council should be proud of to be returning again after COVID-19 and the community gets the full opportunity to participate in local government.

speaker: stephanieasher
text: Thank you, Councillor AIKEN. Any other comments on this item?

speaker: kyliegrzybek
text: Councillor GRISBECK. Thank you, Mayor Asher. I think most of it has been said already by my fellow Councillors, so thank you for that. I think we've got to remember that this is a temporary measure and that hopefully by 1 November, we will open the Council Chamber back up again and have those interactions with our community that we expect and as Councillor MANSFIELD has said, that we expect to be held to account for those particular issues. I think the City of Greater Geelong has been a little bit in front of these changes. We've introduced live streaming quite a little while ago and I think it's benefiting us now in this current environment that we have at the moment. The Minister for Local Government did change the rules which we needed to happen, which allows us to meet virtually like this at home at the moment. I think some of these changes that are in this policy reflect the moving nature of the way the environment that we can engage with our community. I, for one, think that this virtual opportunity is really exciting as a mum and as someone that lives not in the CBD, it's actually kind of nice once you finish a Council meeting to go inside and be part of your family instead of having to drive all that way home. That's just something from my perspective but I really think that this opportunity that we're doing this live on the stream tonight is really showing how progressive we are and the idea that we want to remain transparent to our community and that we can live stream from wherever we are is a really good thing. That's probably all I've got, Madam Mayor.

speaker: stephanieasher
text: Well said, Deputy Mayor, thank you. Look, I'll just close in saying that the incidence of COVID-19 and the restrictions has really highlighted some process issues that I think we've all learned a lot from and virtual meetings is one. I think we've also realised that what we would really like to be able to do is have the opportunity to do a hybrid model where we're in the actual Chamber by choice with the public in the gallery but if somebody can't actually attend in person that they can still actually attend virtually and that's something that we'll be working on. That's to make it more inclusive certainly for mums or any parents at home or people who work shifts or people who can't actually get down to City Hall in the CBD at seven o'clock on a Tuesday night which is a time that I think suits nobody. That's one of the things that we're working on from a process point of view and the team has done a great job and a shout out to Jake and Rebecca and the team and Dean for getting the virtual system up tonight. We had a couple of hitches but we're getting there and that's what it's all about. One of the other things with this policy is people do obviously submit their questions in writing and they're due in by 12pm or 12 lunchtime on the day before the Council meeting. Something I've really noticed and it's been highlighted since we don't have people coming into the Chamber at all, we're really dependent on those submissions and what time they arrive and I think sometimes people send them on a Friday or a Saturday and they think that they come straight to us and they actually don't. They go into the team and we often don't see the submissions and the answers and all of that process until the day of the meeting which is an interesting process piece that I think we can improve as well to make sure that the answers are more fulsome and more of a greater quality from a Councillor perspective. The team do a really good job but I think we can contribute there as well. One of the other changes here is that the Chief Executive Officer henceforth will determine how questions and submissions can be read out and answered safely at a Council meeting and that really I suppose highlights the fact that it is an operational issue and the safety of our community is absolutely our number one priority at all times and I'm satisfied that the approach that we're taking with public questions and submissions, although it's not ideal because people aren't there in person just yet, I'm happy to move the fact that this is a pretty good solution in the meantime. So if everybody's happy to vote on this one, I'll put this one to the vote. All those in favour? Those against? Carried. That was the last item for the evening.
